reopen_history.reason: Type B cast defect: TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP(REGEXP_REPLACE(col, offset-strip), "yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss[.SSSSSS]") returns NULL on any shape the pinned format misses (date-only values especially), and TRY_ makes it silent -- those NULLs reach the judge as differing_null_only/gap_shaped, i.e. a parse failure disguised as a FHIR coverage gap at the lower bar. Replace every datetime mapping with a bare TRY_CAST(col AS TIMESTAMP_NTZ). See pathling-sql SKILL.md and MIMIC_NOTES.md:337.

attempt_0004/concept.sql:31 and :41 map Observation.effective_datetime and effective_period_start through CAST(TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP(REGEXP_REPLACE(...), pinned-format) AS TIMESTAMP_NTZ). The offset-aware parser re-renders the instant in spark.sql.session.timeZone and the pinned format silently NULLs any shape it misses (date-only values especially), so the recorded exact match holds only at session zone America/New_York and is not reproducible elsewhere. This is the same defect the first reopen was meant to clear; attempt_0004 still carries it. Replace both with a bare TRY_CAST(col AS TIMESTAMP_NTZ), nothing wrapped around it. The REGEXP_REPLACE at :58-59 is unrelated trailing-zero stripping on quantity_value and must stay. mimic_utils validate-demo now refuses this construction (sql_lint datetime-parser).

Same Observation.id UUIDv5 inversion as icp, plus a REGEXP_REPLACE that guesses how the source value was stringified in order to rebuild the hash input. Refused by sql_lint (resource-id-inversion); UTC-pinned reads plus comparator key_attribution make it unnecessary. The 100% exact match was earned through an opaque-id side channel and is withdrawn.

Downstream SQL-on-FHIR consumers join derived tables on getResourceKey() resource keys, which the port computes internally but drops at the outermost SELECT. The attempt adds the paired key column beside each MIMIC identifier column (subject_id->patient_key, hadm_id->encounter_key, stay_id->icu_encounter_key, specimen_id->specimen_key). Additive and shape-only: both comparison paths project manifest columns explicitly, so no compared value can change. The MIMIC integer columns are retained as the oracle join keys.
reopen_history.superseded_justification: Judge accepted attempt_0006: mimic-fhir/sql/fhir_observation_chartevents.sql:9,67 irreversibly normalizes spring-forward chartevents charttime before writing Observation.effectiveDateTime. The comparator found 287078/287152 identical rows, with 16 key-shift pairs and 32 residual collision losses producing 26 conflicts; the original wall time is unrecoverable by permissible FHIR queries because it survives only in opaque Observation.id identity. All defensible mappings were exhausted and this is the contract's accepted New York DST transformation loss.

reopen_history.reason: [replay:data_rebuild] The MIMIC-on-FHIR warehouse was rebuilt on 2026-08-24 after two upstream data defects were fixed: FHIR resources are now generated under UTC, so wall-clock timestamps are no longer shifted an hour across the spring-forward boundary, and Patient.birthDate is now derived from the anchor year and age rather than from the first transfer. This port was carried forward byte-identical to re-measure it against the corrected data -- do not re-author it. Expect previously accepted divergences to have shrunk or gone; if an hour-wide shift still appears, treat it as a finding and establish why the correction did not reach that path rather than accepting it as an upstream artifact.
reopen_history.superseded_justification: Judge accepted attempt_0007: exhaustive comparator attribution closes all 26 differing_conflict, 48 only_oracle, and 16 only_candidate rows to the upstream America/New_York DST TIMESTAMPTZ normalization at mimic-fhir/sql/fhir_observation_chartevents.sql:9,67. The current port sources Observation.effectiveDateTime, preserves repeated chartevent rows, faithfully applies the canonical MAX pivot including 32 collision effects, uses opaque resource-key equality only, and has no essential loss or residual divergence. 287078/287152 rows are identical (99.9742%); the 26 conflicts are 0.0091% and the 64 key-side findings are consistent with DST-gap rarity.
